skill_drafts.name: Legacy Session Global State Cleanup
skill_drafts.description: Deprecate and remove old global _active_session references from module scope, replacing them with auto-init trace context and legacy session globals. Prevents state corruption and initialization race conditions by consolidating duplicate global session objects into a single authoritative reference.
contraindications: active consumers still depend on old global _active_session API without migration path
legacy API consumers not yet migrated to agentops.start_trace()
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Audit codebase for all global _active_session definitions and references'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Verify auto-init trace context (_client_init_trace_context) is initialized and accessible'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Update atexit handler to reference only new consolidated global'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Add deprecation warnings to old API entry points'}
{'step': 7, 'action': 'Verify no active consumers depend on old global without migration path'}
triggers: atexit handlers reference conflicting session objects
constraints: must maintain backward compatibility during transition period
atexit handler must use only new consolidated globals
all old _active_session references must be explicitly deprecated
cautions: This is an irreversible global state change; requires explicit deprecation sequencing.
Verify all callers have migrated before removing old API.
Test atexit handler behavior under concurrent initialization.
output_contract: Single authoritative global _client_legacy_session_for_init_trace replaces all old _active_session references; atexit handler uses only new globals; no state corruption or initialization race conditions.

metadata.prompt: Identify all old global _active_session definitions in the codebase. Replace references with _client_legacy_session_for_init_trace. Ensure atexit handlers and auto-init trace context use only the new consolidated global. Verify no active consumers depend on the old API without a migration path.

skill_drafts.name: Singleton Instance Deduplication
skill_drafts.description: Remove duplicate class variable definitions (e.g., __instance = None) that appear multiple times in a class definition. Apply when consolidating singleton initialization to prevent accidental re-initialization or state corruption.
applicable_signals: multiple __instance = None declarations in same class
class consolidation or refactoring in progress
contraindications: intentional multiple definitions for version compatibility or feature flags
class uses factory pattern instead of singleton
duplicate definitions serve as fallback or conditional initialization
workflow_steps: Locate all occurrences of __instance = None (or equivalent singleton marker) in the class definition
Identify the primary definition location (typically early in class body)
Verify singleton initialization logic (__new__, __init__) is intact
Run unit tests to confirm singleton behavior is preserved
triggers: class definition contains repeated __instance or similar singleton marker variables at module or class scope
code review or linting detects duplicate class variable assignments
singleton initialization logic is being consolidated or refactored
constraints: do not alter singleton initialization logic or __new__ method
maintain class scope and visibility of remaining definition
cautions: verify no code path depends on the removed duplicate definitions
test singleton behavior after deduplication to ensure no re-initialization occurs
check for any conditional logic that may have relied on duplicate definitions
output_contract: Single __instance = None definition remains in the class; all duplicate declarations removed; singleton initialization logic unchanged; class instantiation behavior verified to match pre-refactor state.

metadata.prompt: Scan the class definition for all occurrences of __instance = None or similar singleton marker variables. Identify and remove all duplicate declarations, keeping only one definition at the appropriate scope (typically at class level, before or after __init__). Verify that singleton initialization logic remains unchanged after deduplication.

skill_drafts.name: Atexit Handler Global Access Pattern
skill_drafts.description: Enable atexit handlers to access and finalize session context by exposing module-level globals (_init_trace_context, _legacy_session_for_init_trace) through static/class methods or module-scoped variables. Use when atexit cleanup requires session state without circular imports or direct object references.
applicable_signals: session cleanup deferred to process exit
circular import risk detected between session and handler modules
contraindications: session cleanup is synchronous and completes before atexit registration
no session state exists at exit time
session object is already garbage-collected before atexit fires
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Define module-level globals at the top of the module', 'detail': 'Create _init_trace_context and _legacy_session_for_init_trace as module-scoped variables, initialized to None or a default state.'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Expose globals via accessor methods if needed', 'detail': 'Optionally wrap globals in static or class methods to provide controlled access and avoid direct global mutation.'}

{'step': 3, 'action': 'Register atexit handler with closure over globals', 'detail': 'In the atexit handler function, reference the module-level globals directly or via accessors. Capture them in a closure if necessary.'}

{'step': 4, 'action': 'Implement safe finalization in the atexit handler', 'detail': 'Check that session object is not None, call finalization methods (e.g., flush, close), and catch exceptions to prevent atexit errors.'}

{'step': 5, 'action': 'Test atexit behavior during module shutdown', 'detail': 'Verify that the handler fires, accesses session state without AttributeError, and completes without raising exceptions.'}
triggers: atexit handler registration is required for session finalization
session object is not directly accessible from atexit scope
module shutdown must flush or close session state
constraints: Module-level globals must be defined once, not repeated in class definitions
Avoid storing session references in multiple global locations; use a single canonical global
Do not rely on instance variables; use class or module scope only
Atexit handler must not raise exceptions; wrap cleanup in try-except
cautions: Global _active_session patterns can cause confusion; prefer explicit _client_legacy_session_for_init_trace naming
Atexit handlers run in reverse registration order; ensure dependencies are ordered correctly
Module-level state may be partially torn down by the time atexit fires; check for None before access
output_contract: Atexit handler successfully accesses and finalizes session state without AttributeError, NameError, or circular import errors. Session cleanup completes before process exit. No unhandled exceptions propagate from the atexit handler.

examples.input: Module initialization with session object and atexit registration required.
examples.output: Module-level _legacy_session_for_init_trace is set; atexit handler is registered and can access it on shutdown.
examples.notes: Typical flow: initialize session → store in module global → register atexit handler → handler accesses global on exit.

examples.input: Atexit handler attempts to finalize session but session is None.
examples.output: Handler checks for None, skips finalization, and returns cleanly without error.
examples.notes: Defensive pattern: always guard global access with None checks in atexit handlers.

metadata.prompt:
To implement atexit handler access to session context:
1. Define module-level globals (_init_trace_context, _legacy_session_for_init_trace) at module scope, not inside class definitions.
2. Expose these globals via static or class methods if encapsulation is required.
3. Copy or reference these globals in the atexit handler registration to avoid scope issues.
4. Ensure the atexit handler can call finalization methods on the session object without AttributeError.
5. Verify no circular imports occur between the session module and atexit handler registration.
